answer: Before admitting agents from the staging lagoon, the protocol tests spatial memory through timed graph queries. An attacker deploying fake personas incurs the verifiable hardware cost of reserving physical memory chips per identity, facing expulsion at the latency ledge. When an agent embarks on a verification voyage across non-compressible pointer graphs, it must stream proofs in real time. A key limitation is that memory bus contention can falsely disqualify honest lightweight agents.
